clue.text: Sovereign possessions ?

parts.note: read plainly, the things a monarch owns; a sovereign is also a gold coin, so it hints at money in the pocket

explanation.surface: A query about what a king or queen owns.
explanation.definitionFit: Land and estates held by the monarch in right of the throne are the state's royal holdings.

clue.text: Type of sportsman who can't stand paddling!

definitions.text: Type of sportsman who can't stand paddling!

parts.words: Type of sportsman who can't stand paddling!
parts.note: seems to describe someone who hates splashing in the shallows, but means one who must stay seated in a narrow boat while using a paddle

explanation.surface: A sportsman who loathes wading at the seaside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can't stand' reads as 'dislikes'; it means literally unable to stand up, since standing would tip the craft over.
explanation.definitionFit: A paddler of a light narrow boat sits or kneels and would capsize by rising to their feet.

clue.text: To argue like this is a crime against humanity

indicators.note: points at the letters just given and says they are to be rearranged in this fashion into a new word

explanation.surface: Someone claims that quarrelling in a certain way is an atrocity.
explanation.walkthrough: The seven letters of 'To argue' are rearranged, signalled by 'like this'.
explanation.definitionFit: An atrocity or gross violation of decency shocks the public, a monstrous wrong against people.

clue.text: A refuge from one's troubles

indicators.note: the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows, across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: Somewhere to escape one's worries.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'oNE'S Troubles'; the clue reads as a single definition, but only 'A refuge' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird's snug home is a shelter, and the word also means any cosy retreat.

clue.text: See 1
Isolated Greek schoolchildren given bursaries for further studies at Oxford?

definitions.meaning: pupils from the Greek island of Rhodes; an island is isolated

definitions.text: given bursaries for further studies at Oxford
definitions.meaning: holders of the scholarship founded by Cecil Rhodes for overseas students at Oxford University

explanation.surface: Island children from Greece win grants to study at Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: Students funded by the Rhodes Trust at Oxford; read literally, pupils who live on the island of Rhodes.

clue.text: Prepare to go forwards in the told of sport?

definitions.meaning: to put clothes into a suitcase before a journey

definitions.text: forwards in the told of sport
definitions.meaning: in rugby the forwards together form the scrummaging unit

explanation.surface: Getting ready to set off, as attacking players do in sport.
explanation.walkthrough: The two senses run together so 'Prepare to go forwards' reads as one phrase; the break is after 'go'.
explanation.definitionFit: Filling luggage readies a traveller; in rugby union the eight forwards are collectively the scrum unit.

clue.text: Newspaper employees no journal can do without

definitions.meaning: staff who check proofs for errors on a newspaper
a magazine needs people who buy and peruse it

explanation.surface: Staff a paper cannot manage without.
explanation.definitionFit: Proof-checkers work at a paper, and every periodical depends on an audience.

clue.text: A far cry from the Tirol

definitions.text: A far cry from the Tirol

parts.words: A far cry from the Tirol
parts.note: 'a far cry' usually means very different from; here it is literally a call that carries a long way, from the Alpine region of Tirol

explanation.surface: Something very unlike the Austrian Alps.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'a far cry from' means 'very unlike'; read literally it is a carrying call heard from Tirol's mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpine herders sing with rapid switches into falsetto, a call that carries across valleys.

clue.text: Trouble arising when the gas ring gets reallocated to the Marines

indicators.note: the letters are given new places, so they are rearranged

parts.note: RM is the abbreviation for the Royal Marines

explanation.surface: Kitchen equipment is handed over to the Royal Marines, causing trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reallocated' rearranges THE GAS RING into GATHERINGS; TO is as written, then RM.
explanation.definitionFit: A brewing tempest is a common image for difficulty building up and about to break.

clue.text: Russian girl seen in action at a Shakespeare festival

indicators.note: the girl's name can be spotted inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A Russian girl is spotted performing at a Shakespeare festival.
explanation.walkthrough: The name runs across 'actioN AT A SHAkespeare'.
explanation.definitionFit: A common Russian female first name, as worn by the heroine of War and Peace.

clue.text: Kind of sea-monster not easy for a fruit-grower to cultivate?

parts.note: an orc is a mythical sea-monster, also a name for the killer whale
hard means difficult

explanation.surface: A sea-monster is troublesome for a fruit farmer to raise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not easy' looks like a comment on cultivation, but it supplies a piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Apple and pear growers tend a plantation of fruit trees.

clue.text: Dash out of 25 maybe

indicators.note: the letters of that answer are put out of order

parts.note: the answer to 25 down, the Siberian river

explanation.surface: Rushing out of something numbered twenty-five.
explanation.walkthrough: 25 down is LENA; 'out' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: Verve and style, a sense of 'dash' meaning flair and panache.

clue.text: Love-torn females that are destined to go on foot

indicators.note: the females are torn open so love can go inside them

parts.note: she is a female, so females are shes
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: Women heartbroken over love, fated to walk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Love-torn' reads as heartbroken; it means SHES torn open by O.
explanation.definitionFit: Footwear is made to be worn over the feet.

clue.text: Good or bad result of a whipping?

definitions.meaning: well-being, as in the public good
a raised mark left on skin by a lash

explanation.surface: Asking whether flogging leads to good or bad.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means welfare (as in 'commonweal') and also a red welt raised on the skin by a cane.

clue.text: Bright young men who achieve rapid success in office

definitions.text: Bright young men who achieve rapid success in office

parts.words: Bright young men who achieve rapid success in office
parts.note: describes clever youngsters who rise quickly at work, and the first word of the two-word phrase suggests rapid movement

explanation.surface: Clever youngsters who are promoted fast.
explanation.walkthrough: This clue covers 15 and 22 together; the second word of the phrase is entered at 22.
explanation.definitionFit: Young high-flyers rising quickly in business or politics are prodigies.

clue.text: Norman 20

parts.note: 20 down is a person with red hair; William II, the second Norman king of England, had a ruddy complexion and a Latin nickname for 'red'

explanation.surface: A man called Norman with a reference number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Norman' looks like a first name; it is the Norman dynasty. William II was nicknamed for his red face or hair.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin nickname of William II, Norman king, meaning red-haired or ruddy.

clue.text: The weed that took all the pastor's pocket-money?

definitions.meaning: a common wild plant of the cabbage family with heart-shaped seed pods
a pastor is a minister who tends his flock, and his money bag holds his cash

explanation.surface: A weed that pinched the minister's spending money.
explanation.walkthrough: A pastor is literally a herdsman of the flock, so his money bag gives the plant's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A common weed with purse-shaped pods, named after a herdsman's pouch.

clue.text: A coloured print to brighten up the home?

definitions.text: A coloured print to brighten up the home?

parts.words: A coloured print to brighten up the home?
parts.note: seems to be a framed picture for the wall, but means a printed cotton fabric for curtains and covers

explanation.surface: A colourful picture to cheer up a house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'print' suggests an art reproduction; here it means a printed textile.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy cotton cloth printed with bright patterns, used for upholstery and curtains.

clue.text: Stiff problem for the man who wants to move a joint of meat out of a fridge?

definitions.meaning: a painful condition in which the arm joint locks

definitions.text: for the man who wants to move a joint of meat out of a fridge
definitions.meaning: a chilled cut of lamb or pork from the forequarter is hard to shift

explanation.surface: Someone struggling to lift a cold joint out of the freezer.
explanation.definitionFit: Adhesive capsulitis stiffens the arm at its upper joint; literally, an iced cut of lamb.

clue.text: Supremely important Communist ginger-nut?

parts.note: red is the colour and nickname of communists
head as an adjective means chief or principal

explanation.surface: A leading Communist with ginger hair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ginger-nut' looks like a biscuit, but 'nut' is slang for the head, so it is a red-haired person.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with auburn or carrot-coloured hair; nut is slang for the head.

clue.text: Free deed, though treated with scorn

annotationWithheld.why: Clue 'Free indeed, though treated with scorn': RID (free) goes in DEED, so the one printed word 'indeed' is both the container indicator 'in' and the fodder DEED
annotationWithheld.clue: Free deed, though treated with scorn

clue.text: See 15

annotationWithheld.why: Clue reads only 'See 15': the second word of 15's two-word answer, but the file does not group it with 15-down, so it has no clue of its own

clue.text: Rapacious topsails?

parts.note: the predatory birds of prey share a name with the light upper sails flown high on a ship

explanation.surface: Greedy sails at the top of a mast.
explanation.walkthrough: The birds are known as rapacious scavengers, and a ship's highest light sails share their name.
explanation.definitionFit: Scavenging birds of prey, and also the lightest upper sails set in fine weather.

clue.text: Broken lamps that might be brought into service

definitions.text: that might be brought into service

indicators.note: the word lamps is smashed and its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Damaged lights that might yet be reused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'service' means a church service, not repair work.
explanation.definitionFit: A sacred song from the Bible is sung or read in church worship.

clue.text: Got right inside a picturesque cavern

indicators.note: the letter for right goes inside the word got

explanation.surface: Someone gets inside a pretty cave.
explanation.definitionFit: A poetic word for a grotto, an ornamental cave.

clue.text: Little Nell crossing the wastes of Siberia

definitions.meaning: a pet form of Helena, as Nell is of Helen
the great river that flows north through Siberia

explanation.surface: Dickens's Little Nell crossing the Siberian wilderness.
explanation.walkthrough: Little Nell is the heroine of Dickens's The Old Curiosity Shop, but here it means a short girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name shortened from Helena, and a major Siberian river flowing to the Arctic.

clue.text: He rings mother up first

indicators.note: the mother piece comes first, before the rings
in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: ma is a familiar word for mother
rings look like the letter O, so rings are Os

explanation.surface: A man telephones his mother before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rings' seems to mean telephones; it gives OS. 'up' turns MA to AM, placed 'first'. 'He' is the Old Testament prophet.
explanation.definitionFit: An Old Testament prophet, a man who gives his name to a book of the Bible.

clue.text: Three changes to put on in addition

indicators.note: the word three changes its letter order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Three outfit changes to put on as well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put on' looks like dressing; it is the link joining wordplay to a definition, a formal word for 'besides'.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal word meaning besides or moreover, added to something mentioned.

clue.text: Temporary ban on light meals for Moslems

definitions.text: Temporary ban on light meals for Moslems

parts.words: Temporary ban on light meals for Moslems
parts.note: suggests a ban on snacks, but means no eating at all during daylight for a month

explanation.surface: A short-term bar on snacks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'light meals' reads as snacks; it means meals in the light of day.
explanation.definitionFit: The ninth month of the Islamic calendar, when the faithful fast from dawn to sunset.

clue.text: Misreads a special order for troops on parade?

indicators.note: the letters of the first word are put into a new and different sequence

explanation.surface: A special parade-ground command is misread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order' looks like a military command; it means the letters' new sequence.
explanation.definitionFit: Pistols and bayonets worn at the belt are carried by soldiers on parade.

clue.text: The marsh plant furthest from the northern frontier?

parts.note: the point furthest from north is south, S
an edge is a border or frontier

explanation.surface: A marsh plant at the most southerly boundary.
explanation.walkthrough: The southern border is read as S plus EDGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A grass-like plant that grows in wet ground and fens.
